steps.title: Run read-only discovery of the source account
steps.description: Run `hermes inventory aws` with a dedicated read-only cross-account role (Describe/List/Get only, ExternalId required). Discovery is agentless and does not depend on IaC state; the source may have been built by hand. Terraform state and CloudFormation stacks only annotate managed_by. Secret values are never read.
steps.rollback: Nothing to roll back; discovery is read-only. Remove the discovery role when the migration ends.
validation: Inventory metadata.read_only is true
Every entry in inventory.gaps is triaged: accepted, or discovery re-run with broader read-only access
Inventory regions cover every region the source account uses (check billing by region)
risks: Denied or throttled describe calls leave gaps; undiscovered scope is migration risk
Discovery adds API load on the source account and can be throttled at large scale

steps.title: Assess the inventory and sign off scope
steps.description: Run `hermes migrate assess` against the target provider. Review blockers, every resource classified manual-review or compatibility unknown, the dependency waves and the draft_spec. Record scope decisions (migrate, rebuild, retire, keep in place) in docs/decisions.
steps.rollback: Re-run the assessment; nothing is changed by it.
validation: Every blocker has an owner and a decision
draft_spec reviewed by a human before it is used
risks: Capability equivalence in the catalog is not operational equivalence; owners must review differences per resource
Cost estimates are indicative list-price ranges, not quotes

steps.title: Optional: adopt the source into IaC without changing it
steps.description: `hermes adopt aws` generates import blocks from the inventory into a separate source workspace with its own state. The engine imports existing resources; nothing is created, changed or deleted on the source. This is IaC adoption, not migration: source and target state stay isolated, and resource identity never moves between them. Review any generated configuration (-generate-config-out is experimental and can write sensitive values).
steps.rollback: Delete the source workspace state; imported resources are unaffected.
validation: Plan in the source workspace shows no changes after import
risks: A later apply in the source workspace with drifted configuration would modify production; plans there must show no changes before any apply

steps.title: Create the target resource hierarchy, billing and budgets
steps.description: GCP: organization, folders and one project per environment, billing account link, budgets with alerts. Alibaba Cloud: Resource Directory with member accounts or resource groups per environment, budgets/cost alerts. Apply organization-level guardrails (allowed regions, no service-account key creation on GCP, control policies in Resource Directory).
steps.rollback: Delete the empty projects/accounts and detach billing.
validation: Budgets and alert recipients exist for every environment
Allowed-region policy matches the regions in the Platform spec
risks: Organization policies applied later can block migration tooling (for example service-account key creation or external IP restrictions)

steps.title: Bootstrap the Hermes state backend on the target
steps.description: Create the remote state bucket with infra/bootstrap/<provider>/state-backend (versioned, encrypted, private, deletion-protected). The bootstrap is applied once per project with an explicit approval.
steps.rollback: Remove deletion protection and delete the empty state bucket; never delete a bucket that holds state.
validation: State bucket has versioning, encryption and public-access prevention enabled
Locking works (two concurrent plans: the second waits or fails)
risks: Losing state orphans resources; versioning and deletion protection must stay enabled

steps.title: Set up human and CI access to the target
steps.description: Federate workforce identities (SSO) instead of creating local users, define a break-glass procedure, and give CI a federated workload identity (GCP Workload Identity Federation, Alibaba Cloud RAM role with OIDC) so no long-lived keys exist.
steps.rollback: Remove the federation configuration and role bindings.
validation: No user-managed service-account keys or RAM user AccessKeys exist for CI
Break-glass access tested and logged
risks: Long-lived access keys created for convenience become a secret-sprawl problem

steps.title: Provision customer-managed keys and the target network
steps.description: Write the Platform spec (start from the assessment draft_spec), then `hermes plan` and `hermes apply --approve <plan-id-prefix>`. Choose a network CIDR that does not overlap any source VPC CIDR from the inventory, because hybrid connectivity needs routable, distinct ranges.
steps.rollback: hermes destroy --approve <plan-id-prefix> --confirm-environment <env> (keys enter their provider-specific deletion waiting period).
validation: Target CIDR does not overlap any AWS::EC2::VPC cidr in the inventory
hermes plan shows no destructive actions on re-run (idempotent)
risks: Overlapping CIDRs make hybrid connectivity impossible without NAT
Scheduling key deletion makes all data encrypted with that key unrecoverable after the waiting period

steps.title: Enable audit logging and log retention on the target
steps.description: GCP: Admin Activity audit logs are always on; enable Data Access audit logs where required and route them to a locked log bucket. Alibaba Cloud: create an ActionTrail trail delivering to SLS or OSS. Match or exceed the retention obligations the source CloudTrail setup meets.
steps.rollback: Disable the additional audit log configuration (Admin Activity logs cannot be disabled on GCP).
validation: A test administrative action appears in the audit log within minutes
Retention configured to the required period
risks: Data Access audit logs can be high volume and costly

steps.title: Document access patterns
steps.description: For each table/collection: keys, secondary indexes, item sizes, read/write rates, consistency requirements, TTL, transactions, conditional writes and streams. Access patterns, not schemas, decide the target (document store, wide-column store, relational).
validation: Every query pattern listed with expected latency and volume
risks: Proprietary APIs (DynamoDB, DocumentDB subsets of MongoDB) hide behaviour applications depend on

steps.title: Design the target data model
steps.description: Choose the target and record the decision (docs/decisions), including consistency semantics, indexing limits and cost model differences.
validation: Design reviewed against every access pattern
risks: Consistency differs: eventual by default on some sources, strong on some targets, and region/cluster dependent

steps.title: Introduce a data access layer with dual-write support
steps.description: Put reads and writes behind an interface with feature flags for read-from and write-to per backend.
validation: Flags switch backends in a test environment

steps.title: Enable export and change capture on the source
steps.description: DynamoDB: enable point-in-time recovery (needed for export to S3) and a stream with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES. DocumentDB/MongoDB-compatible: enable change streams. Redis-compatible stores: plan snapshot export (replication commands are restricted on managed services).
steps.rollback: Disable the stream / PITR after migration.
validation: Stream enabled and readable by the CDC consumer
risks: PITR and streams add cost on the source

steps.title: Record what each workload needs
steps.description: From the inventory: image references, ports and protocols, CPU/memory, environment variable names (values are not collected), secret references, task/pod IAM roles, health checks, autoscaling, sidecars, volumes, schedules and event triggers. Flag workloads that accept non-HTTP inbound traffic (raw TCP/UDP), which serverless HTTP runtimes do not serve.
validation: Each workload has protocol, resources, identity and dependencies recorded
risks: Configuration injected at runtime from sources outside the task definition is invisible to discovery

steps.title: Decide rehost or re-platform for VM-hosted containers
steps.description: Docker workloads on EC2 managed by configuration management (for example Ansible) can be rehosted (Compute Engine / ECS VMs, same playbooks, fastest, keeps VM operations) or re-platformed to the target container runtime (Cloud Run / SAE, same images, needs the host-level settings — volumes, host networking, cron, log and monitoring agents, secrets on disk — moved into the image, the platform or the Platform spec). Record the choice per workload.
validation: Every host-level dependency in the playbooks has a target equivalent
risks: Playbooks often configure state on the host (files, certificates) that a re-platform silently drops

steps.title: Remove provider coupling from the application
steps.description: Read endpoints and names from the Hermes binding contract (HERMES_* variables), use provider-neutral client libraries behind an interface where possible, emit telemetry with OpenTelemetry over OTLP (the AWS X-Ray SDKs and daemon entered maintenance mode on 2026-02-25 with end of support on 2027-02-25, so this work is needed on AWS too), and use CloudEvents for event payloads. Ship these changes while still on AWS.
validation: Application runs on AWS with configuration only from HERMES_* and OTEL_* variables
risks: Hidden SDK usage (S3 presigned URLs, SQS long polling, IAM auth tokens for RDS) surfaces late

steps.title: Document the current resource
steps.description: Configuration (inventory attributes), usage, data volume, dependencies (relationships) and owner.
validation: Owner, usage and dependencies recorded
risks: Resources classified 'other' may be inventory gaps in disguise

steps.title: Evaluate options
steps.description: Options: managed target service (catalog alternatives and differences), portable open-source software on the target container runtime, keep in place on AWS with hybrid connectivity, or retire. Include lock-in, operations effort and cost.
validation: At least two options compared

steps.title: Record the decision
steps.description: Write an ADR in docs/decisions and add a catalog entry if the pattern will recur.
validation: ADR approved by the service owner

steps.title: Extract the source configuration from the inventory
steps.description: Use the inventory attributes (non-secret configuration) and the catalog differences to write down what must be reproduced: sizing, parameters, retention, thresholds, routing.
validation: Each resource in scope has a target configuration recorded
risks: Inventory completeness: partial resources may be missing settings

steps.title: Assess buckets and objects
steps.description: Per bucket: total bytes and object count (from storage metrics or inventory reports), storage classes (archived classes need restore), versioning, encryption (SSE-S3 / SSE-KMS key), Object Lock, lifecycle rules, replication, event notifications, bucket policies, CORS, static website hosting, requester pays, and object metadata/tag usage.
validation: Size, count and storage-class distribution recorded per bucket
risks: Object count, not bytes, often dominates transfer time and request cost for small objects

steps.title: Decide what is copied
steps.description: Transfer tools copy current versions by default. Decide whether noncurrent versions are needed (Storage Transfer Service can copy specific versions listed in a manifest, which needs s3:GetObjectVersion), whether object tags and ACLs matter (Storage Transfer Service does not preserve them; new S3 buckets have ACLs disabled by default), and how retention obligations under Object Lock are re-established on the target.
validation: Scope decision recorded per bucket
risks: Source timestamps are not preserved by Storage Transfer Service, so age-based lifecycle rules restart from the copy date
Legal holds and retention modes do not travel with the objects

steps.title: Restore archived objects before transfer
steps.description: Objects in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive cannot be read until restored. Restore them in batches (S3 Batch Operations) before transfer, or exclude them. Restores incur retrieval charges and temporary storage.
steps.rollback: Restored copies expire automatically after the requested number of days.
validation: No in-scope object remains in an archived state without an active restore
risks: Deep Archive restores take hours; bulk restores take longer and cost more than the transfer itself

steps.title: Grant read-only access for the transfer service
steps.description: Create an IAM role in the source account trusted by the transfer service (federated identity preferred over access keys) with s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObject (and s3:GetObjectVersion when a manifest names versions) on the in-scope buckets, plus kms:Decrypt on SSE-KMS keys. Alibaba Data Online Migration uses an access key for the source (long-lived credential): create a dedicated IAM user limited to these actions, enter the key directly in the Alibaba Cloud console, never store it in Hermes artifacts, files or tickets, and delete it in the decommission workflow.
steps.rollback: Delete the role or IAM user and its keys.
validation: Access works for listed buckets and is denied for any other bucket
risks: Long-lived access keys for the transfer are a secret that must be stored and deleted properly

steps.title: List secrets, consumers and rotation from metadata
steps.description: Use the inventory (names, KMS keys, rotation settings, tags, uses-secret relationships). Discovery never reads values and Hermes never stores them.
validation: Each secret has an owner and a list of consumers
risks: Secrets embedded in environment variables or code are invisible to the inventory

steps.title: Classify each secret: re-issue or copy
steps.description: Prefer re-issuing on the target (new database passwords for the new database, new API keys from the issuer) over copying. Copy only credentials that cannot be re-issued, and rotate them after cutover so only one copy remains valid.
validation: Every secret labelled re-issue or copy
risks: Copied credentials remain valid in two clouds

steps.title: Map messaging semantics per queue/topic
steps.description: For each topic, queue and subscription record: standard vs FIFO, deduplication, message size (SQS and SNS accept up to 1 MiB payloads; Pub/Sub up to 10 MB; check the SMQ limit, which is far lower), visibility timeout (Pub/Sub ack deadline is at most 600 s), delay queues, retention, dead-letter configuration and max receive count, filter policies, and delivery targets other than queues (email, SMS, HTTP, Lambda). Streams: shard/partition counts, retention and consumer checkpoints.
validation: Every queue/topic has a target mapping or a documented redesign
risks: Visibility timeouts above 600 s, per-message delays and very large messages have no direct Pub/Sub equivalent
Pub/Sub dead-lettering accepts 5-100 delivery attempts; smaller max receive counts must be raised

steps.title: Make consumers idempotent and provider-neutral
steps.description: Both sides deliver at least once (exactly-once delivery on Pub/Sub applies only to pull subscriptions within a region). Consumers must tolerate duplicates and reordering during the switch. Use CloudEvents for payloads and the HERMES_TOPIC_* / HERMES_SUBSCRIPTION_* bindings for names.
validation: Replaying the same message twice produces no duplicate side effects (test)
risks: Consumers that rely on FIFO order across the switch see out-of-order messages

Options AWS<->Alibaba Cloud: IPsec-VPN dual-tunnel with BGP, or Express Connect through a connectivity partner. Bulk object data may not need the private link at all (for example the Storage Transfer Service managed private network).
validation: Throughput requirement and chosen option recorded in docs/decisions
risks: IPsec tunnels have per-tunnel throughput limits; aggregate several tunnels with ECMP for higher throughput
Data sent over a VPN still incurs AWS data transfer out charges plus hourly VPN connection charges

steps.description: Choose private ASNs for both sides, link-local /30 inside-tunnel CIDRs, and confirm the target VPC CIDR does not overlap the source VPCs. Advertise only the prefixes needed for migration traffic.
validation: No overlap between advertised prefixes on each side
risks: Advertising broad prefixes can attract production traffic onto the tunnel

When they carry device command-and-control traffic they are safety-critical: build the target relay alongside the source, run both in parallel for a dual-running window, move devices in small cohorts with a tested fallback to the old relay, and never include them in a bulk cutover.
steps.rollback: Devices fall back to the source relay, which stays up for the whole dual-running window.
validation: Each device cohort reports healthy command-and-control sessions through the target relay before the next cohort moves
risks: Loss of command-and-control connectivity to devices in the field
Device firmware or configuration updates are needed to change endpoints or credentials

steps.description: Provision with Hermes (workloads.database). validation: Target version >= source version; extensions installed; roles created
risks: Destination automated backups and PITR are suspended by Google DMS until promotion

steps.description: Public ACM certificates generally cannot be exported (only certificates requested as exportable, available since 2025-06-17, at extra cost), so issue new certificates on the target. steps.rollback: Remove the authorization records and delete unused certificates.

steps.rollback: Stop the consumer / disable dual-write; the source stays authoritative.
validation: CDC lag below the agreed threshold
risks: Out-of-order application of changes without version checks corrupts data

Pulling images across clouds at runtime adds egress cost, latency and a dependency on the source.
steps.rollback: Delete the copied images from the target registry.
validation: Digest on the target equals the digest on the source for every image
risks: Signatures and attestations stored as separate artifacts are not copied unless the tool copies referrers
Registry egress from AWS is billed as data transfer out

steps.title: Execute using the standard workflows
steps.description: Compose the migration from standard workflows (object-storage for data, traffic-cutover for endpoints, decommission for retirement). Any step that touches the source is treated as modifying it and needs approval.
steps.rollback: Follow the rollback of each composed workflow step.
validation: Each executed step has a validation result
risks: Ad-hoc steps skip validation

steps.title: Warm caches and baselines
steps.description: Caches start empty. Warm them by lazy loading under controlled traffic or by replaying a read workload, and expect extra load on the database behind them during the first hours. Monitoring baselines (anomaly detection) also need time to learn.
validation: Cache hit ratio on the target approaches the source ratio before full cutover
risks: A cold cache at cutover can overload the database (thundering herd)

steps.rollback: Delete the copied objects from the target bucket.
validation: Transfer job completed with zero failed objects, or every failure triaged
risks: AWS data transfer out and request charges accrue on the source bill

steps.title: Run incremental synchronizations
steps.description: Schedule repeat runs that copy only new or changed objects. Do not enable deletion of destination objects missing from the source until the final sync, and never enable deletion of source objects after transfer.
validation: Each run's changed-object count trends toward the application's write rate
risks: Delete-propagation options misconfigured can delete data
